section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Language of Binary
section_1.content: Briefly introduce binary as a base-2 system using only 0 and 1. Explain that just as decimal (base-10) uses powers of 10, binary uses powers of 2. Use a visual representation of 3 light bulbs (representing 4, 2, and 1) to show how any number can be formed.
section_1.example: Visual: 3 bulbs. If the 4-bulb and 1-bulb are ON (101), the value is 5. If all are ON (111), the value is 7.

section_2.title: The Towers of Hanoi Challenge
section_2.content: Introduce the puzzle: 3 rods and N disks of different sizes. Rules: Only one disk moved at a time; a larger disk cannot sit on a smaller one. Pose the question: What is the minimum number of moves to solve it for 3 disks?
section_2.example: Animation: A robotic arm moving disks from Rod A to Rod C, following the rules.

section_3.title: Connecting Moves to Binary Counting
section_3.content: Reveal the magic link: As you count in binary (1, 2, 3, 4...), the changes in binary digits correspond exactly to disk movements. The bit that changes tells you which disk to move. If the 1st bit changes, move disk 1; if the 2nd bit changes, move disk 2.
section_3.example: Table: Count 001 (Move Disk 1), 010 (Move Disk 2), 011 (Move Disk 1), 100 (Move Disk 3).

section_4.title: The Power of 2^n - 1
section_4.content: Explain why the total moves for 'n' disks is always 2^n - 1. Connect this back to the binary counting limit: a 3-bit binary number can count up to 7 (2^3 - 1).
section_4.example: Visual: For 3 disks, 2^3 - 1 = 7 moves. Animation shows the binary counter ticking from 001 to 111 as the disks reach the target rod.

section_5.title: Application: The Cosmic Clock
section_5.content: Apply the concept to a real-world scale. Mention the Legend of Brahma: 64 golden disks. Calculate the time required to finish (at 1 move per second, it would take over 500 billion years). This highlights the exponential nature of binary growth.
section_5.example: Animation: A turtle and a hare. The hare (exponential growth) quickly outpaces the turtle (linear growth) as the number of disks increases.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Moves follow 2^n - 1.", "3 disks need 7 moves total.", "Binary limits match Hanoi moves."]
        self.setup_layout("The Power of 2^n - 1", lecture_lines)
        
        # Objects
        formula = MathTex("2^n - 1").set_color(BLUE)
        disk_label = Text("n = 3").set_color(YELLOW)
        moves_label = Text("Moves = 7").set_color(GREEN)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B2")
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.place_at_grid(disk_label, "D2")
        self.place_at_grid(moves_label, "E2")
        self.play(FadeIn(disk_label), FadeIn(moves_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        binary_label = Text("Binary 111 = 7").set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(binary_label, "C5")
        self.play(Write(binary_label))
        self.wait(2)
